title: Credit Builder Accounts Early-Closure Late-Fee Relief and the Part of the Installment Paid
content:
The early-closure late-fee relief on a Credit Builder account is scaled by how much of the oldest unpaid installment has been paid. The scaling acts on the amount the relief share gives on the late fee, and the relief is rounded to the cent after it.

## Rule

- When a payment has been posted toward the oldest unpaid due date and the account shows an amount past due above zero but below the monthly payment, the relief is scaled by the part paid, that is the monthly payment less the amount past due, divided by the monthly payment.
- When the account shows an amount past due of the monthly payment or more, or an amount past due above zero with no payment posted toward the oldest unpaid due date, the relief is halved (multiplied by 0.5).
- When the account shows no amount past due, the relief keeps its full amount.

The oldest unpaid due date is the next due date the account shows; a payment posted toward it is a payment entry whose installment due date is that date. The amount past due and the monthly payment are read from the account record.

| Payment posted toward the oldest unpaid due date | Amount past due | Relief |
|---|---|---|
| yes | above 0.00, below the monthly payment | scaled by the part paid |
| no | above 0.00, below the monthly payment | halved |
| either | the monthly payment or more | halved |
| either | 0.00 | full amount |

## Hypothetical figures

Monthly payment 100.00; the relief share gives 3.00 on the late fee:

| Account | Scaling | Relief |
|---|---|---|
| a 60.00 payment posted toward the due date; amount past due 40.00 | 100.00 less 40.00, divided by 100.00: 0.6 | 1.80 |
| no payment toward the due date; amount past due 100.00 | halved | 1.50 |
| no amount past due | full | 3.00 |
